why: A business motion report of December 1965 holds a Resolved record, a time-stamped all-caps heading and a footnote between rules that quotes the motion. The heading and the footnote were credited to the mover; the footnote lines are editorial notes, and an all-caps heading is no speech, so no row has a speaker.
title: SUSPENSION OF STANDING ORDERS
subtitle: (Business Motion)
html:
Parliament No:1
Session No:1
Volume No:24
Sitting No:2
Sitting Date:13-12-1965
Section Name:MOTIONS
Title:SUSPENSION OF STANDING ORDERS (Business Motion)
MPs Speaking:Dr Toh Chin Chye (Deputy Prime Minister);


Column: 43



2.47 p.m.
SUSPENSION OF STANDING
ORDERS
(Business Motion)


    Resolved, "That, notwithstanding the Standing Orders, the Motion of Thanks to the Yang di-Pertuan Negara* which has been set down for today be deferred to the 14th December, 1965."-[Dr Toh Chin Chye].
*The Motion reads as follows:

    "That the following Address in reply to the speech of the Yang di-Pertuan Negara be agreed to:-

    We, the Legislative Assembly of Singapore, express our thanks to the Yang di-Pertuan Negara for the speech which he delivered on behalf of the Government at the opening of the present Session of this Assembly."
